question: If $A=[a_{ij}]$ is a $3\times3$ diagonal matrix such that $a_{11}=1$, $a_{22}=5$ and $a_{33}=-2$ then $|A|$ is:
explanation:
Step 1 Understand the layout of a diagonal matrix. A square matrix is a diagonal matrix if all entries outside the principal diagonal are zero. We can write out the full matrix as: $A = \begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\ 0&5&0\\ 0&0&-2\end{bmatrix}$.

Step 2 Recall the determinant property specific to diagonal matrices, which states that the determinant is simply equal to the product of all its main diagonal entries.

Step 3 Compute this product using the given scalar components: $|A| = a_{11} \times a_{22} \times a_{33} = 1 \times 5 \times (-2) = -10$. This evaluates exactly to option B.
